item.title: 📜 Agent Hunt paper published at PAAR'26
item.description: Our paper Agent Hunt: Bounty Based Collaborative Autoformalization With LLM Agents, by Chad E. Brown, Cezary Kaliszyk, and Josef Urban, has been published in the proceedings of the Workshop on Practical Aspects of Automated Reasoning (PAAR 2026), held as part of FLoC 2026 in Lisbon, Portugal. The paper explores large-scale autoformalization of algebraic topology using a simulated bounty marketplace, where multiple LLM agents propose formal lemmas, attach bounties, and compete to discharge proof obligations, scaling collaborative formalization in a decentralized fashion.

item.title: 🎤 Invited Talk at SCML-2026
item.description:
Prof. Cezary Kaliszyk gave an invited talk at SCML-2026, the conference on Symbolic Computation and Machine Learning, held July 6–8, 2026 in Hagenberg, Austria.

His talk, “Formalization and Automated Reasoning in the Age of LLMs”, was presented on Monday, July 6, and discussed how large language models are reshaping formalization and automated reasoning. The slides are available here.

item.title: 📜 New Publications
item.description:
We are happy to announce a series of new papers from our team, all accepted for publication. The work spans two intertwined themes: large-scale LLM-assisted autoformalization of mathematical textbooks, and machine learning guidance for higher-order automated theorem proving. See our Publications page for details.

  • Learning-Guided Higher-Order Automated Reasoning for Isabelle/HOL. We present higher-order extensions of ENIGMA and Deepire — the two prominent learning-guided reasoning systems for the E and Vampire provers — and evaluate them on a large Isabelle/HOL corpus emulating Sledgehammer, observing consistent improvement across the board.
